title: Filming: John Lennon and Yoko Ono in New York City | 1980
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono were filmed in several Manhattan locations on 26 November 1980.

The shoot was directed by Ethan Russell, who had worked as a photographer on The Beatles’ Let It Be. He had been contracted by Ono to work on the new project, which was for promotional purposes.

It’s been like a reunion for us these last few weeks. We’ve seen Ethan Russell, who’s doing a videotape of a couple of the new songs, and Annie Leibovitz was here. She took my first Rolling Stone cover photo. It’s been fun seeing everyone we used to know and doing it all again – we’ve all survived.
John Lennon, 5 December 1980
Rolling Stone

The shoot began with Russell filming Lennon and Ono walking through Central Park, after which they moved to the Sperone Westwater Fischer art gallery at 142 Greene Street in SoHo.

At the gallery a white bedroom set had been assembled, along with a fake staircase, white stepladder, and Ono’s perspex Apple sculpture. Also present was photographer Allan Tannenbaum.

Lennon and Ono changed into kimonos before undressing and pretending to copulate on the bed. Several takes were recorded before filming paused for dinner at 9pm. Afterwards more shots were filmed, and the shoot ended at around 11pm.
